root_cause: The Escape key's cancel event becomes non-cancelable after repeated activations, causing the dialog to close unexpectedly when keyboard:false. This occurs because the native cancel event (which fires only for modal dialogs) loses its cancelable property, so preventDefault() has no effect and the dialog's default close action proceeds.
repair_strategy: Modify the Escape keydown listener in DialogBase._addDialogListeners to prevent default and return early when keyboard:false, regardless of modal status, thereby consuming the Escape key before it triggers a cancel event.
expected_accessibility_effect: Escape key will no longer dismiss the dialog when opened with keyboard:false, allowing users to remain focused on the OTP input and complete the transfer without accidental closure.
functional_risks: Consumers who rely on the cancel event firing for Escape when keyboard:false will no longer receive that event.
verification_requirements: Pressing Escape any number of times must not close the dialog when keyboard:false.
Pressing Escape must still close the dialog when keyboard:true.
The dialog must still be dismissible via the Cancel button and via submitting a correct six‑digit OTP.
